forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Dacorum housing depot project £1.5m over budget as capital delivery falters
news_drafts.lead: Dacorum council faces a £1.5m overspend on the Paradise Depot, a housing repairs scheme budgeted at £7.2m but now projected to cost £8.7m — a 21% overspend and the largest single capital overspend in the entire programme. Work is well underway with nearly £1m already spent. The overspend comes as the council's housing investment programme more broadly stutters: a scheme to build new council homes budgeted at £4.4m is now forecast to spend only £1m this year, a 77 per cent shortfall. Meanwhile, the council has discovered the Forum's electricity meter was faulty for years; repair work completed in April means annual utility bills will jump by £200k. The findings emerged from the Finance and Resources scrutiny committee's review of quarter-one spending.

findings.paper_title: FINAL - Financial Monitoring Q1 2026.27 Cabinet Report
findings.headline: Revenues & Benefits administration faces £82k structural funding gap after government moved to centralised funding approach
findings.detail: Central government moved from ad hoc grants to centralised funding allocations such as Revenue Support Grant. This structural reform has created a £82k budget pressure. The position will be reviewed as part of 2027/28 budget setting.
findings.matters: This reflects a government funding reform affecting local authority finance structures and suggests similar pressures other councils may face.
findings.quote: Central government have looked to move to a more centralised approach to funding, wrapping up individual grant pots into corporate funding allocations such as the Revenue Support Grant. This has created pressures on budgets such as these.

findings.paper_title: FINAL - Financial Monitoring Q1 2026.27 Cabinet Report
findings.headline: 2026/27 savings delivery 90% on track at £3.350m of £3.487m, with £34k garden waste and £103k garage income delayed
findings.detail: Of £3.487m agreed 2026/27 savings, £3.350m are on track. £34k garden waste and £103k garage rental income are delayed. The garage income pressure mirrors the £136k income shortfall reported elsewhere in the forecast.
findings.matters: 90% delivery is generally positive, but the 10% at risk includes garage income which is also forecasting as an operational pressure, creating interdependency risk.
findings.figures: £3.487m total savings, £3.350m on track, £34k garden waste and £103k garage rental delayed
findings.quote: Of the £3.487m of savings, £3.350m are deemed to be on track. £34k of garden waste is deemed to be delayed as this may be met by in year receipts, and £103k of garage rental income is delayed as detailed earlier in this report whilst plans are put in place to meet this budget gap.

findings.paper_title: FINAL - Financial Monitoring Q1 2026.27 Cabinet Report
findings.headline: General Fund capital programme £2.116m slippage at quarter 1; HRA capital £1.913m underspend
findings.detail: General Fund shows £2.116m slippage across multiple schemes including £1m DIP (not expected to require investment this year), £327k Parking Solutions, £121k Durrants Lake, and £125k Old Town Hall. HRA reports £1.913m underspend relating to unspent contingency on new build development programme.
findings.matters: Capital slippage at 18% of revised General Fund budget suggests delivery pace issues or timing differences that could impact longer-term borrowing requirements.
findings.figures: General Fund £2.116m slippage (18% of £11.608m revised budget); HRA £1.913m underspend
findings.quote: General fund capital budgets are reporting slippage of £2.116m relating to the following: £1m Dacorum Investment Partnership (DIP) – it is not expected that capital investment will be required for the DIP in this financial year.

findings.paper_title: FINAL - Financial Monitoring Q1 2026.27 Cabinet Report
findings.headline: HRA responsive repairs forecast to overspend by approximately £200k; detailed review underway to determine if temporary or structural
findings.detail: Responsive repair expenditure trends indicate a potential year-end overspend of approximately £200k, currently offset by underspend in disrepair compensation claims. Officers are undertaking a detailed review to assess whether this represents temporary fluctuation or sustained trend, with findings expected in coming weeks.
findings.matters: This emerging operational pressure is partially masked by other underspends, making underlying trajectory uncertain until the review findings are available.
findings.figures: ~£200k overspend potential, offset by disrepair compensation underspend
findings.quote: The HRA is currently forecasting cost pressures within responsive repairs, with expenditure trends indicating a potential year-end overspend of approximately £200k against the repairs and maintenance budget.

findings.paper_title: FINAL - Financial Monitoring Q1 2026.27 Cabinet Report
findings.headline: Car parking income £136k below target due to rising garage void rates, despite strong on-street performance
findings.detail: On-street parking revenues have performed strongly in Q1, generating a £177k surplus. However, garage rental income is forecast £136k below target due to rising void rates. This £136k pressure represents only 3% of the annual garage income target of £4.390m.
findings.matters: Parking income contains material variance across asset classes requiring active management, with garage performance offsetting on-street gains.
findings.figures: £177k on-street surplus, £136k garage pressure, £4.390m annual garage income target
findings.quote: Garage income is forecast to be £136k below target at year-end, reflecting increasing void rates across the garage portfolio and the associated loss of rental income.

daily_post.headline: HRA financing costs ratio 22.20% budgeted, -21.90% at Q1 estimate, a 44 percentage point movement
daily_post.lead: The HRA is a material liability; a swing this large in financing costs indicates a significant change in strategy or assumptions that a lender would need to understand.
